clue.text: Injured by swindle in currency

indicators.note: in tells us the swindle sits inside the currency word

parts.note: the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries
a trick is a swindle or con

explanation.surface: Someone hurt after falling for a money scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Stricken describes someone struck down, wounded or afflicted, so it can stand for hurt.

clue.text: Novice rewrites scripture without a second thought

indicators.note: rewriting the word scripture rearranges its remaining letters
without says some letters of scripture are dropped before the shuffle

explanation.surface: A beginner edits holy writ without pausing to reconsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes PS from SCRIPTURE, leaving CRITURE, which 'rewrites' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit is a newcomer to an army or organisation, a beginner.

clue.text: Can the first to bid force an entry? Yes

definitions.text: Can the first to bid force an entry? Yes

parts.note: a can is a tin
in bridge the opener is the player who makes the first bid

explanation.surface: A bridge question: may the opening bidder barge into the auction?
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the gadget: it forces its way into a can.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen tool cuts open a sealed can, forcing a way inside.

clue.text: Gave off bubbles, induced by electrical discharge

indicators.note: by places the discharge word next to the word for induced, ahead of it

parts.note: a spark is a brief electrical discharge
led means induced or brought about

explanation.surface: Something fizzed when an electric current set it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne that sparkled was effervescent, fizzing with bubbles.

clue.text: Twisted spire — rare sight in annals of the church

indicators.note: twisted tells us the letters of the next three words are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked church steeple is an unusual thing to see.
explanation.definitionFit: The parish register is the record book of baptisms, marriages and burials kept by a church.

clue.text: Artist with bronzed look from Malacca

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a tan is a bronzed skin colour

explanation.surface: A sunburnt painter coming back from Malaysia.
explanation.walkthrough: Malacca is a cane made from a palm stem; RATAN is a variant spelling of rattan.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malacca is a walking stick of palm cane, the kind of cane rattan supplies.

clue.text: Under a pound, say? Not so much for getting blotto!

clue.text: No ceiling for assured involved in violence

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters left are mixed
in a down answer the ceiling is the top letter, so assured loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone confident gets dragged into a brawl with the roof off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No ceiling for' removes the A from ASSURED, leaving SSURED, which 'involved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion by threats or force, the compulsion of violence.

clue.text: Film is one in a hundred for bringing the East nearer to us

definitions.text: bringing the East nearer to us

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film

indicators.note: in puts the one inside a hundred

parts.note: a ton is a hundred
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A movie that's one in a hundred brings Eastern audiences closer to us.
explanation.definitionFit: Westernisation is the adoption of Western ways, pulling Eastern cultures towards ours.

clue.text: Who better than an artist to recount unusual story?

definitions.text: Who better than an artist to recount unusual story?

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist

indicators.note: unusual tells us the word recount appears in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A question about who should tell a strange tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a skilled teller of anecdotes, the ideal narrator of a strange tale.

clue.text: It got a smile from the young lady of Riga

definitions.text: It got a smile from the young lady of Riga

parts.words: It got a smile from the young lady of Riga
parts.note: the limerick about the young lady of Riga who rode on a big cat: they came back with the lady inside, and the smile on the face of the beast

explanation.surface: Who made the girl from Latvia smile?
explanation.walkthrough: In the limerick the smile ends up on the animal's face, not the lady's.
explanation.definitionFit: In the limerick the striped cat ate the lady and wore her smile.

clue.text: Ladies who should be placed near the fire

definitions.text: Ladies who should be placed near the fire

parts.words: Ladies who should be placed near the fire
parts.note: British slang for attractive women, and also a griddle cake you toast at the fire

explanation.surface: A sexist suggestion that women belong by the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: The British word is old slang for women seen as sexually attractive and also a spongy teacake toasted before the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for desirable women, and a teacake that is toasted.

clue.text: Star, being minor, is not shadowed

parts.note: the sun is a star
lesser or less means minor

explanation.surface: A small star that casts no shade.
explanation.walkthrough: With no sun out, nothing casts a shadow, so the definition is a cryptic angle on dull weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunless sky casts no shadows, since shadows need direct light.

clue.text: Great envy gnawed away at the heart

indicators.note: at the heart says the letters sit in the middle of the words Great envy

explanation.surface: Jealousy eating someone up from within.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gnawed away has been consumed, chewed up.

clue.text: Go to the country to climb round mountain range

indicators.note: round says the climbing word goes round the range

parts.note: to rise is to climb
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: Heading for the countryside to scale peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruralise is to adopt country ways, to retire to rustic life.

clue.text: Foreign nobleman has a country accent

parts.note: a land is a country
the grave is an accent mark, as in è

explanation.surface: An aristocrat from abroad who speaks with a rural twang.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German count with territorial rule, a nobleman abroad.

clue.text: Lent is brought forward

definitions.meaning: money lent is ..., as in a loan
brought forward, moved earlier or put ahead

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: money advanced is a loan, and an advanced date is moved earlier.

clue.text: Making black tea to take round

parts.note: char is slang for tea
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: Brewing a cuppa to hand round.
explanation.definitionFit: Charring is scorching or burning something until it is blackened.

clue.text: The natural place to find poor Tabitha…

indicators.note: poor suggests Tabitha is in a sorry state, so her letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Where to find a needy girl named Tabitha.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 21-down with its ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural home of a plant or animal.

clue.text: Sound produced by needles is brilliant

indicators.note: Sound tells us we want a word that is said like the one meaning produced by needles

parts.note: knitted, made with knitting needles

explanation.surface: Needles clicking produce a lovely noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitid is a literary word for shining or glossy, bright.

clue.text: …but not the sort of way to find Lucy

definitions.text: …but not the sort of way to find Lucy

parts.words: …but not the sort of way to find Lucy
parts.note: Wordsworth's Lucy poem says she dwelt among ways no one walked; continuing from 19-down, those ways are not the walked kind

explanation.surface: Following on: where you would not look for Lucy.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's 'She dwelt among the untrodden ways' is about Lucy; the ways she lived in were untrodden, so not this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A trodden path is well walked, the opposite of the untrodden ways of the poem.

clue.text: Old plane runs into mouth of volcano

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, rickety aircraft
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An old aircraft flies into a volcano's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is the bowl-shaped opening at the top of a volcano.

clue.text: Polish girl with German complaint

parts.note: to rub is to polish
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from Poland with a gripe about Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella is the disease commonly called German measles, an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Ship in river south of the Equator

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of puts the river letter below the Equator word

parts.note: the Line is a sailors' name for the Equator

explanation.surface: A boat in a river in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship.

clue.text: Soldier's rejected girl and married woman in Italy

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the soldier word is turned round

parts.note: GI is an American soldier; GI's gives GIS
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A soldier dumps a girl and marries an Italian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, like Mrs.

clue.text: "I'm God", said one-eyed artist

indicators.note: one-eyed means one I is taken out, eye sounding like the letter

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A painter with a single eye claims divinity.
explanation.walkthrough: One-eyed removes one of the two I's from TITIAN; the quote marks dress the deity as boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the elder gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Scandinavian animal in charge to left and right

parts.note: the same abbreviation repeated, on the other side
an eland is an African antelope
the same abbreviation repeated, on the other side

explanation.surface: A Nordic beast takes command on all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to left and right' puts IC on both sides of ELAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Icelandic describes people or things from Iceland, a Nordic nation.

clue.text: Modest about dressing

parts.note: re means about or concerning
tiring is an archaic word for dressing, from attire

explanation.surface: Shy about getting clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retiring is shy and self-effacing, reserved.

clue.text: Wrote and put in a pound

definitions.meaning: wrote, set down with a pen
shut up in an enclosure, as livestock in a fold

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: written in ink, and confined in a pen or enclosure for animals.
